title: locality-weighted-reservation-stabilizer-and-burst-signal-denoiser
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduces a locality-weighted reservation stabilizer to reduce oscillation across pool topologies, and a burst-signal denoiser to filter short noisy spikes. Adds telemetry for per-pool denoised-utilization and adjustment-rate. Backwards-compatible config defaults; rollout controlled via feature flag.
commits: init: add stabilizer plugin scaffold and config plumbing
alg: implement EWMA + spectral denoiser for burst signal
autoscaler: locality-weighted reserve delta computation and safety caps
telemetry: expose pool_denoised_util and reserve_adjust_rate metrics
charts: add feature flag and defaults to dedicated/fleet chart
tests: integration tests for noisy-burst scenario and deterministic localities
fix: lint and flake fixes (formatting + increased integration timeout)
description:
Motivation: In multi-pool dedicated fleets we observed frequent reservation oscillation where pools with overlapping tenant locality react to the same short spikes. That produces unnecessary churn (decommits/reallocations) and transient latency spikes. This PR introduces two coordinated improvements: a locality-weighted reservation stabilizer that amortizes reserve deltas across correlated pools, and a burst-signal denoiser to filter short high-frequency noise before it influences autoscaler decisions.

Summary of changes and rationale: Adds a Stabilizer plugin (pkg/autoscaler/stabilizer) that computes a locality-weighted expected delta for reservations. The plugin consults a lightweight locality correlation matrix (derived from recent connection scatter by tenant) to scale per-pool adjustments so that highly correlated pools take proportionally smaller individual deltas and the system instead performs a coordinated reservation step. The denoiser (denoiser.go) combines an EWMA short-term filter with a lightweight spectral high-frequency attenuator to remove sub-second microbursts from the utilization signal used by the autoscaler. Together these reduce false-positive reserve churn and smooth utilization telemetry.

Checklist:
- [x] Stabilizer plugin implementation with config knobs and safety caps
- [x] Denoiser algorithm with unit tests for corner cases
- [x] Telemetry endpoints and Grafana dashboard hints (docs/observability.md)
- [x] Chart toggle and safe defaults (feature flag off by default)
- [x] Integration tests simulating noisy bursts and cross-pool locality
- [x] Updated autoscaler metrics and e2e assertions

Commits: (high level)
- init: scaffold stabilizer and config wiring
- alg: EWMA + spectral denoiser implementation with parameterized time constants
- autoscaler: integrate stabilizer output into reserve delta decision path, add deterministic safety caps
- telemetry: create pool_denoised_util and reserve_adjust_rate metrics, tag by pool_id and locality_bucket
- charts: expose feature flag and reasonable defaults (window=30s, alpha=0.2, correlation_threshold=0.45)
- tests: add integration scenarios and increase timeouts for deterministic runs

Files changed (high level):
- pkg/autoscaler/stabilizer/*: core algorithm and config parsing, small helper functions for correlation scoring
- pkg/autoscaler/locality/*: utilities to compute recent locality scatter and compact correlation vectors
- pkg/telemetry/*: metric registration and lightweight exporters (statsd/prom)
- cmd/allocator/main.go: feature flag wiring and plugin registration
- charts & deploy: feature flag defaults, documentation snippets
- integration: noisy_burst_test and locality_mesh_test verify both reduction in reservation churn and preserved throughput SLOs

Testing and CI: Unit tests cover denoiser frequency response and stabilizer safety caps. Integration tests run in the CI noisy-burst matrix; initial run produced a flaky integration failure due to an optimistic timeout in noisy_burst_test (test harness sometimes needs an extra 8s under CI load). After increasing the harness timeout and fixing a small race in the locality snapshotter, CI passed all lanes (lint/build/unit/integration).

Review conversation (high level):
- Miguel Santos: "Nice pattern — can we make the default correlation window configurable and add a short circuit when cross-correlation is below X so we don't pay compute cost?"
  - Aisha: "Added correlation_window_secs to the config and short-circuit when max_correlation < 0.15; documented in autoscaler-config.md."
- Priya Desai: "Denoiser looks promising; please add a regression test for a 200ms microburst and ensure we don't drop real 5s bursts."
  - Aisha: "Added an integration case and unit tests that assert denoiser passes 5s bursts but filters 200ms spikes; also tuned default alpha."
- Evan Liu: "Telemetry tags look good, but watch cardinality of locality_bucket."
  - Aisha: "Buckets capped to 12 and only created when correlation exceeds threshold; added note in observability.md."
- Priya (approve): "Approved after test additions and docs."
- Miguel (approve): "Looks good. Minor comment about comments in weights.go resolved."

CI/Checks:
- CI lanes: gofmt, golangci-lint, unit tests, integration (noisy-burst matrix), helm lint
- First CI run: golangci-lint failure (ineffassign) + flaky integration timeout
- Fixes: addressed linter suggestions, increased integration timeout, fixed race in locality snapshot cache
- Final CI: all lanes green

Performance and rollout plan:
- Default: feature flag off. For early canaries enable in 1-2 pools with differing locality topologies.
- Metrics to watch during rollout: pool_denoised_util (trend), reserve_adjust_rate (spikes/h), allocation_churn_rate, tenant_latency_p50/p95.
- If reserve_adjust_rate or allocation_churn_rate drop without throughput regressions, rollout to more pools.

Migration and backward compatibility: All config knobs have sensible defaults so there is no required migration for existing clusters. The stabilizer is additive — if feature flag is off behavior is unchanged.

Merge: Squash-and-merge with the following commit message: "stabilizer: locality-weighted reservation stabilizer + denoiser; telemetry and tests".

Follow-ups (tracked separately in Linear):
- instrument a debug-mode CSV export for locality correlation snapshots (ENG-2401)
- explore a machine-learned correlation estimator if current scatter windows are noisy (ENG-2410)
- small UX work for the Console to visualize denoised-util trends (PM-501)

Notes: This PR intentionally keeps the denoiser lightweight (no FFT libs added) to avoid increasing binary size; the spectral attenuator uses a small sliding DFT approximation that is sufficiently precise for our microburst filtering needs. The locality correlation uses a compact hash-bucketed sketch so memory is O(pools * sketch_size).
